claims.explanation: Carmofur is a thymidylate synthase (TYMS) inhibitor and acid ceramidase (ASAH1) inhibitor; its selectivity likely reflects dependence on TYMS-mediated dTMP synthesis and on ASAH1-driven ceramide detoxification, with additional contribution from oxidative-stress and apoptosis pathways. Lines with high TYMS or ASAH1 expression, or with loss of p53/apoptotic or redox buffering, should be more sensitive, while high DHFR or nucleotide-salvage capacity may protect.

features.basis: carmofur is a TYMS inhibitor and transcriptional response resembles TS inhibitors (raltitrexed)
carmofur is a potent acid ceramidase inhibitor and this property is essential to its antiproliferative effects
p53 loss may reduce apoptotic response to DNA damage and ceramide stress
high DHFR supports nucleotide salvage and reduces dependence on TYMS
carmofur treatment upregulates CASP2 in the virtual cell, suggesting apoptotic priming
BAX upregulation in virtual cell indicates mitochondrial apoptosis engagement
p21 induction in virtual cell suggests DNA-damage/replication-stress response
SESN1 upregulation in virtual cell indicates oxidative-stress response
survivin downregulation in virtual cell suggests loss of apoptosis inhibition sensitizes
mitotic cyclin downregulation in virtual cell suggests cell-cycle arrest contributes to response
CDC20 downregulation in virtual cell suggests mitotic catastrophe pathway
GALC deficiency increases psychosine/ceramide load, potentially enhancing ASAH1 dependence
